phase_2_searches.outcome: 50 combinations found across trains 12781 and 17301 (up to 5 segments). Revealed that DFS enumeration order let the per-train cap cut off simpler combinations; enumeration was then improved to iterative deepening (fewest segments first).

phase_2_searches.search: MYS->DWR 2026-11-27 3A GN (CHEAPEST) - run B (final, improved enumeration)
phase_2_searches.outcome: 25 combinations, best first: train 12781 MYS->UBL->DWR, 2 segments, both CONFIRMED_AVAILABLE, 1400 INR total, while the 12781 direct ticket is WAITLISTED (GNWL88/WL57, 855 INR) - the core RailRoute AI value proposition demonstrated on live data. Second segment boarded 2026-11-28 (overnight day-offset handling verified on the real API).

phase_2_totals.note: Monthly free-plan quota effectively exhausted; real-API work for this phase is complete.

key_learnings: Availability varies sharply by date: 2026-11-26 had no fully confirmed same-train combination in SL or 3A, while 2026-11-27 3A had many.
The per-segment boarding-date semantics (day offsets) are essential and work on the live API: overnight segments must be queried with the next calendar date.
Batch endpoint + deduplication saved 98 of 175 planned queries in the final run (56% saved).
Same-train segmentation is confirmed real: a waitlisted direct ticket (12781 GNWL88/WL57) coexists with fully available MYS->UBL and UBL->DWR segments on the same train run.
Segmented fares exceed direct fares on real data: 1400 vs 855 INR (+63.7%) on 12781 3A.
A full two-train exploration costs roughly 150 credits on this route (16-stop window); budgets matter on the free plan.
